sections.h2: Which ways of selling fast are open in Cleburne, TX?
sections.html:
Owners in a hurry usually sell straight to a cash buyer, while owners with time often go through an agent. A direct sale skips showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal, so closing depends mostly on clear title.

  • Cash buyer: suits inherited houses, tenant-occupied rentals, deferred repairs and foreclosure dates.
  • Agent: suits a house in good repair and a seller with room in the schedule.
  • By owner: suits someone comfortable with contracts and buyer screening.

Cleburne is the Johnson County seat, and the county appraisal district keeps its office in the city.

sections.h2: How did Cleburne grow around the railroads?
sections.html:
Cleburne began as a railroad and wagon-road town, and that background explains much of what makes it different from newer Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs. The Handbook of Texas places the city on U.S. Highway 67, thirty miles south of Fort Worth. The site sat near the earliest county road and had a good water source on West Buffalo Creek. It became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867, when a central county seat was needed to replace Buchanan, and the town was named for a Confederate general. It incorporated in May 1871.

Rail made the town. A railroad line from Fort Worth through Cleburne to Temple opened in 1881, and in 1898 and 1899 the Santa Fe built its central machine shops here, which helped double the population in the 1890s. The population was 683 in 1870, 3,727 in 1890, 12,820 in 1920, and 26,005 in 2000. The same entry names Lake Pat Cleburne, the Layland Museum in the old Carnegie Library building, and the Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Station nearby as a major employer.

Transport kept layering on. A spur to Egan opened in 1902, the "Boll Weevil" line ran from 1904 to 1924, an interurban from Fort Worth served the city from 1912, and a local streetcar ran from 1911 to 1917. A Carnegie Library opened in 1904 and a junior college operated here from 1909 to 1919. In the 1920s all four city banks failed and a 1922 Santa Fe strike deepened the slump, and the population was 10,558 by 1940. A Civilian Conservation Corps camp built Cleburne State Recreation Park, which opened in 1941.

After 1945 nearness to the Dallas-Fort Worth region brought steady growth: 22,205 residents by 1990 and 26,005 in 2000. The Handbook also names Lake Pat Cleburne, the Layland Museum in the old Carnegie Library building, and the Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Station nearby as a major employer.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Cleburne property tax values?
sections.html:
Johnson County values come from the Central Appraisal District of Johnson County at 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne. The posted hours are 8:00am to 4:30pm on weekdays, with a drop box in the front door, and the phone is (817) 648-3000. Exemption questions go to exemptions@johnsoncad.org.

The district posted that certified 2026 appraisal data became available for download on August 10, 2026. It also reported a 2026 software upgrade with a period of dual data entry, so confirm any exemption on your account with the office itself instead of trusting a screen.

The statewide calendar behind a Johnson County bill: valuation and the tax lien date fall on January 1, homestead notices of value go out around April 1, and the protest deadline is May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. Bills show up around October 1, and unpaid tax is delinquent after January 31.

sections.h2: Who can answer a Cleburne owner's value or protest questions?
sections.html:
The appraisal district lists separate inboxes: customerservice@johnsoncad.org for general questions, exemptions@johnsoncad.org for exemptions and arb@johnsoncad.org for the review board. It also links a Taxpayer Liaison Officer, a role the Tax Code requires in counties with populations above 120,000, who helps taxpayers with access to district functions.

An owner can ask the district to deliver notices electronically, since Tax Code Section 1.085(a-1) requires a tax official to honor that request. That helps a seller who has moved out of the house but still gets the property's notices at the old address.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Cleburne homeowner or buyer claim?
sections.html:
School districts give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with extra school relief for older or disabled owners, and the Comptroller prints disabled veteran brackets running from $5,000 to $12,000 by rating. A veteran rated 100 percent disabled can get a total exemption on a homestead.

File with the appraisal district before May 1. A buyer who moves in after January 1 can often claim the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller never held it.

sections.h2: What should I check on permits and records before selling in Cleburne?
sections.html:
Ask the City of Cleburne's building inspections office whether any permit on your address is open or unfinished, and request the record in writing so you can hand it to the title company.

sections.h2: How does Texas foreclosure work for a Cleburne house?
sections.html:
Texas lenders with a power of sale in the deed of trust can foreclose at a courthouse auction without suing, which for a Cleburne house means Johnson County. The borrower has 20 days from receiving the default notice to catch up.

The sale notice must reach the borrower at least 21 days ahead and also be posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk. If the lender sues afterward over a shortfall, the suit must come within two years. Selling before the auction may protect your equity, so act early if a notice has arrived.

sections.h2: What if the Cleburne house is inherited or has a tenant?
sections.html:
Each of these has its own Texas rule.

  • Inherited: four years to probate a will; a muniment of title can move title when no administration is needed; a small estate affidavit requires $75,000 or less outside homestead and exempt property, plus agreement among all heirs.
  • Tenant: 3 days of written notice, a justice court filing, then a 6-day wait after judgment before a writ of possession; an appeal to county court is due within 5 days.

Tell the buyer about each issue at the start. The title company will want proof of authority to sell, such as a court order or recorded affidavit.

faqs.q: Where is the Johnson County appraisal district office?
faqs.a: At 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne, with weekday hours of 8:00am to 4:30pm and a phone line at (817) 648-3000. A drop box sits in the front door.

faqs.q: How old is the city of Cleburne?
faqs.a: Cleburne became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867 and incorporated in May 1871, according to the Handbook of Texas. It replaced Buchanan as the Johnson County seat.

faqs.q: What is the school homestead exemption in Texas?
faqs.a: The Comptroller prints $140,000 for school districts, with an additional $60,000 for owners who are older or disabled.

faqs.q: How much notice comes before a Texas foreclosure auction?
faqs.a: At least 21 days, and only after the 20-day reinstatement window that follows the default notice. Auctions happen on first Tuesdays.

faqs.q: Does a Cleburne house with repairs still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is, and sellers disclose known problems. An open permit or code issue is the item most likely to need attention before closing, so ask Building Inspections what is on file.
